prompt: A wheelchair ramp is $10$ ft long along the slope and rises at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the ground. How high is the top of the ramp, in feet?
hint: The $10$ ft slope is the HYPOTENUSE, and the height is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle.

hints.text: The $10$ ft slope is the HYPOTENUSE, and the height is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: a $4$ ft slope at $30^\circ$ rises $\frac{1}{2} \times 4 = 2$ ft, because $\sin(30^\circ) = \frac{1}{2}$. Same move, bigger slope.

explanation: Label first: the ramp itself is the hypotenuse ($10$ ft), and the height is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle.

alternativeExplanations.title: Half the hypotenuse
steps: In every $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle, the side opposite $30^\circ$ is exactly half the hypotenuse.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check the size
steps: The height must be smaller than the ramp itself, so the answer has to be under $10$ ft.
A gentle $30^\circ$ ramp should rise only a modest amount.
$5$ ft fits both checks, while an answer like $20$ ft would be impossible.
